inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London on Saturday to protest the far-right, coming together under the Together Alliance in a broad coalition of trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies. This follows just six months after one of Britain's largest-ever far-right demonstrations and arrives weeks before key local elections. To me this turnout represents communities pushing back against the deep structural inequalities and institutional failures that have allowed discrimination and hate to spread, threatening vulnerable groups and workers alike. It's a clear demand for real reform to root out the historical injustices fueling division and to protect labor rights and minority communities from rising bigotry.

To me this turnout shows communities standing together against the deep structural inequalities and institutional failures that have let discrimination and hate spread, putting vulnerable groups and workers at risk. It's a strong demand for real reform to dismantle the historical injustices driving division and to defend labor rights and minority communities from rising bigotry.
